headline: 14 killed as Saudi Aramco helicopter crashes in Ras Tanura
summary: The crash occurred on Saudi Arabia's eastern coast on the Gulf, with the cause of the incident still unknown.
details: A helicopter belonging to the Saudi oil giant Aramco crashed on Sunday in Ras Tanura, located on the eastern coast of Saudi Arabia on the Gulf.
The state news agency reported that 14 Saudi nationals were killed in the crash, which occurred at 6am local time.
Saudi authorities have launched a full investigation to determine the exact cause of the crash, as the cause remains unknown at this time.
The incident happened shortly after Aramco had resumed crude oil loadings at its Ras Tanura terminal on Friday, after a nearly four-month halt.
Saudi Arabia, the world's largest oil exporter, has recently increased oil and gas output and exports to move cargoes ahead of an interim deal to halt the war between the US and Iran.

headline_marked: 11 dead as [[civilian plane crashes in France]]
headline: 11 dead as civilian plane crashes in France
summary: A light aircraft carrying skydivers killed all 11 people on board, including instructors and students, in one of the country's deadliest light aircraft accidents.
details: A civilian aircraft carrying skydivers crashed near the eastern French town of Tomblaine on Sunday, killing all 11 people on board.
The victims include five instructors, five students, and the pilot, according to Yves Seguy, the prefect of the eastern department of Meurthe-et-Moselle.
The German-registered aircraft crashed in a grassy area near the runway of the Nancy-Essey aerodrome, close to a residential area and two roads.
Local authorities confirmed that there were no bystanders among the victims.
Medical and psychological support teams are providing care for relatives of the victims and witnesses at the airfield.
A technical investigation has been opened by the deputy public prosecutor in the eastern city of Nancy to determine the cause of the crash.
caption:
11 people, including skydivers and their instructors, killed in a tragic plane crash in France.

A civilian aircraft carrying skydivers crashed near the eastern French town of Tomblaine on Sunday, killing all 11 people on board.

The victims include five instructors, five students, and the pilot, according to Yves Seguy, the prefect of the eastern department of Meurthe-et-Moselle.

The German-registered aircraft crashed in a grassy area near the runway of the Nancy-Essey aerodrome, close to a residential area and two roads.

Local authorities confirmed that there were no bystanders among the victims.

Medical and psychological support teams are providing care for relatives of the victims and witnesses at the airfield.

A technical investigation has been opened by the deputy public prosecutor in the eastern city of Nancy to determine the cause of the crash.
